reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the Communication structure report, resource-review context, deterministic aggregate, R4/R6 Communication StructureDefinitions for the affected paths, and the supplied direct/shared behavior context. No direct behavior findings include `Communication`; shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings were considered only as context, per the contract.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `Communication` is trial-use/FMM 2, so the compatibility burden is neutral rather than strong. That lowers the presumption against breaking changes, but does not make central payload, reason, workflow-traceability, or protocol/provenance changes unimportant.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Communication keeps its identity, but R6 introduces targeted hard breaks around payload content, reason, instantiation links, and basedOn target validation; migration is partially unavoidable, while low-cost preservation still matters.

reasoning.thesisMd: `Communication` is not removed or replaced, and most of the resource shape remains recognizable. The migration burden comes from a small number of semantically important local remodels: text payloads must move from `contentString` to `contentCodeableConcept.text` or another representation, `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` collapse into `reason` `CodeableReference`, protocol instantiation links disappear, and `basedOn` changes from a broad `Reference(Resource)` to a finite request-resource list.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: This is a **moderate targeted remodel**, not a whole-resource redesign. There are no new local mandatory fields, no resource identity break, and no direct Communication-specific operation/search/HTTP break. However, a realistic R4 Communication migration cannot be handled by validator regeneration alone when instances use common text payload content or reason fields; those require explicit transforms and, in some cases, mapping policy.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A migration program is likely needed for implementations that exchanged populated R4 Communications, especially because payload content is the communicated message itself. That does not make additional break prevention pointless: preserving optional legacy fields or widening a choice type would directly reduce old-valid/new-invalid failures without changing the resource identity or forcing a competing resource family.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest low-cost preservation candidates are retaining `payload.contentString` as a deprecated choice while adding `CodeableConcept`, and retaining `instantiatesCanonical`/`instantiatesUri` as deprecated optional elements or providing an explicit same-resource replacement. By contrast, keeping both old reason fields and new `reason` would create parallel representations needing precedence rules, and keeping `basedOn` as `Reference(Resource)` would weaken the R6 goal of computable request-like targets.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct behavior findings whose `affectedResources` include `Communication` were present. The 11 shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings remain relevant to generic server/client migration planning, but they are not Communication-specific evidence and were not used to make this resource-level structural conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The independent review agrees with the deterministic aggregate's overall posture: `Partial` major migration, `moderate-targeted-remodel`, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`. The reasoning here gives more weight to the qualitative centrality of `payload.content[x]` and to the avoidability of removing string payloads and instantiation links, rather than relying on the raw count of four hard breaks.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The structural deltas are high-confidence because the affected R4/R6 StructureDefinition elements were checked directly. Prevalence, committee rationale, and final R6 resolution remain less certain because the review used the supplied ballot package and reports rather than external change-note history.

findingConsiderations.title: Communication.payload.content[x] removed string content and added CodeableConcept content
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most important Communication-specific break. `payload.content[x]` carries the communicated content, and R4 `contentString` is likely a natural representation for simple messages. R6 can support coded payloads without necessarily invalidating existing string payloads, so retaining `string` as a deprecated choice appears standards-review-worthy.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 reasonCode and reasonReference were merged into Communication.reason CodeableReference
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This creates a real instance-shape and generated-model migration from two R4 arrays into repeated `CodeableReference`. It contributes materially to the migration program, but the R6 model has a coherent datatype goal; the main need is clear mapping guidance rather than necessarily preserving all three fields in base.

findingConsiderations.title: Protocol instantiation elements were removed from Communication
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The removed optional summary elements preserve protocol, guideline, questionnaire, or external-definition linkage. Because they are optional non-modifier provenance links, keeping them as deprecated elements would likely be a low-cost way to preserve R4 instances and audit/workflow meaning.

findingConsiderations.title: Communication.basedOn reference targets were narrowed from any Resource to named request resources
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can reject R4 instances whose `basedOn` points outside the R6 finite request-resource list. It is a local migration concern rather than a resource-redesign driver because R4 already described the element as an order/proposal/plan relationship, and the R6 change makes that intent computable.

findingConsiderations.title: Sender and recipient reference targets were widened for R6 participants
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 instance break: R6 preserves the R4 sender/recipient target sets and adds new targets. It matters only for R6-to-R4 conversion or older clients consuming new R6 data.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This and related Resource-level operation removals can affect generic servers that expose operations on Communication instances, but the finding is assigned to `Resource`, not specifically to `Communication`, so it does not change the Communication resource-level structural judgment.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Shared search-parameter metadata changes may affect conformance tooling and generic search clients across resources. They are relevant implementation context, but they are not a Communication-specific behavior break.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit `Communication.payload.content[x]`: consider retaining `string` as a deprecated choice alongside `CodeableConcept`, or provide explicit normative migration guidance for `contentString` to `contentCodeableConcept.text`.
Revisit the removal of `instantiatesCanonical` and `instantiatesUri`; if they remain removed, define an explicit replacement or extension mapping so protocol/provenance linkage is not lost silently.

Publish concrete migration rules for `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` to `reason` `CodeableReference` and for out-of-list `basedOn` targets, since these are local migration chores once the R6 remodel is accepted.

caveats: Direct Communication behavior findings were absent; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context was not scored as Communication-specific.
Prevalence and rationale assessments are based on supplied local reports and package definitions, not external ballot discussion records.
The R6 source is 6.0.0-ballot4, so final publication changes could alter this review.
